findings.reason: every other implementable section carries a followup, and without one the section that answers the eviction finding is unreachable and the memo store keeps growing.
findings.text: §13 is added as `implementable` but no followup names it: the last open followups are `f-tchhab-008` (§8), `f-tchhab-011` (§11) and `f-tchhab-012` (§12), so the roadmap has no invocation that reaches §13

findings.reason: the node would have to invent the directory and kind name the sweep must target, and §13 has no declared wait to hold it until §6 lands.
findings.text: §13's Why says "`plan_review._snapshot_evidence` now persists one file per distinct snapshot content digest through the persisted-memo helper", but no such code is in the tree: `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` calls neither `persisted_memo` nor any store helper (`grep -rn persisted_memo reckon/crew/plan_review.py` → none; `_snapshot_evidence` at line 877 only reads an existing snapshot), and the section that adds it, `a-read-costs-what-changed` §6, is declared `implementable` at its reviewed head `5be11339a0e6`; the plan's own `plan-standalone` (line 23) says it "waits on none". A node dispatched on §13 today finds no memo directory and no cache kind to name

findings.reason: the case is unsatisfiable as written, so the node either fails its own done-when or satisfies it by writing the file in the test, which proves nothing about a read.
findings.text: §13's done-when requires the gc pass to keep "one read inside it", but the rule it borrows keys on mtime: `_orphan_ledger_indexes` reads `index.stat().st_mtime` (`reckon/crew/gc.py:429`) and `_write_persisted_memo` only writes (`reckon/metadata_index.py:1963,1974`), so reading a memo file never moves its mtime and an entry read a minute ago is swept on age alone; nothing in the declared write paths (`reckon/crew/gc.py` and the new test) can make a read visible, because a read-touch would have to live in `metadata_index.py`

findings.reason: a node reading "size rule" literally would add a byte cap that deletes entries inside the age window, contradicting the next sentence's promise that a recently read entry is kept.
findings.text: "the same age and size rule it applies to the pick-input cache" names a size rule that does not exist: `_orphan_ledger_indexes` (`reckon/crew/gc.py:395-441`) applies one threshold, `LEDGER_INDEX_UNRECORDED_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 7` (`gc.py:213`), and only to an index recording no ledger path; sizes are reported per row and never thresholded, and `RUN_DIRECTORY_SIZE_LIMIT` (`gc.py:221`) bounds a measurement walk rather than retention

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §13's "keeps one read inside it" case cannot be satisfied by the mtime rule it borrows, and nothing in its declared write paths can make a read visible to that rule.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — no gate output is placed in a scratchpad or node-local path; the run directory and repository test paths are the only destinations named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filename and the section's prose name a mechanism, with no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §13 states as present fact a persisted memo store that no code in the tree produces, and it attributes a size rule to the pick-input cache sweep that does not exist.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §13 names one deliverable, one sweep in `garbage_collect`, with one measure.
